$2,000 Raise in Canada: How Much Do You Really Keep?
Will a Raise Put You in a Higher Tax Bracket? (Canada 2026)
yt.description:
Worried a raise will push you into a higher tax bracket? In Canada, a higher bracket never taxes your whole income. Each rate only taxes its own slice.

Example: with $60,000 of taxable income, the first $58,523 is taxed federally at 14% and only the last $1,477 at 20.5% (2026 rates). Real example, Manitoba 2026: a raise from $58,000 to $60,000 adds $318 federal tax, $238 Manitoba tax and $152 CPP + EI, so you keep $1,292 of the $2,000.

One real exception: income-tested benefits like the Canada Child Benefit shrink as family income rises (reduction starts above $38,237 of adjusted family net income for July 2026 – June 2027). On benefits? Run your numbers with a professional.

Sources: CRA 2026 tax rates; CRA T4127 (2026); CRA Canada Child Benefit. Examples only; general information, not tax advice.
